item.description: Enterprise agentic AI systems exchange contextual information across functional modules, creating governance challenges when information crosses operational and organizational boundaries. item.title: The Rise of Language Models in Mining Software Repositories: A Survey
item.description: The Mining Software Repositories (MSR) field focuses on analyzing the rich data contained in software repositories to derive actionable insights into software processes and products. Mining repositories at scale requires techniques capable of handling large volumes of heterogeneous data, a challenge for which language models (LMs) are increasingly well-suited. item.title: Uncertainty-Guided Counterfactual Sensor Selection and Safety-Gated Recognition for Autonomous Sensing Agents in IoT Systems
item.description: Autonomous IoT systems rely on distributed sensing, but sensor faults and communication loss can leave multichannel evidence incomplete or unreliable. Their agents must therefore classify measurements, assess evidence sufficiency, select a sensor to reacquire, and hand off unsafe decisions. item.title: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information
item.description: Many real-world decisions require teams to integrate information distributed across participants. Yet AI agents are still primarily trained and benchmarked in isolation. We introduce TeamGym, an environment for evaluating and training language model-based agents on team decision-making problems constructed from real-world legal, finance, medical, and software engineering corpora. item.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: Memory helps LLM-based multi-agent systems reuse experience, but stored advice can be flawed or applied in the wrong situation. Team-level success or failure alone cannot reliably show whether a memory needs correction or should not have been used. We propose DiscernMem, a training-free framework that improves both memory quality and memory use. item.title: Bounds on user repair after context loss in AI handoffs
item.description: Long-running artificial intelligence (AI) conversations can lose permissions, commitments, or goals when they cross model and context boundaries. This theoretical paper asks when bounded system recovery makes external user repair necessary. We propose a provenance-bearing register of governing constraints and derive a lower bound combining graded continuity shortfall with unrecoverable hard constraints. item.description: Graph-structured representations of text data have become foundational across machine learning, yet it remains unclear how to systematically construct a graph from a given dataset for a target task. item.description: Abstract Applications of narrative theories using large language models (LLMs) deliver promising methods in automatic story generation and understanding tasks. item.title: An agentic framework for intelligent clinical laboratory medicine
item.description: Clinical laboratory medicine is fundamental to healthcare yet remains an underrecognized frontier for artificial intelligence. We propose LabARIA, a human-supervised multi-agent framework that coordinates laboratory data, quality management, workflow optimization, and operational intelligence. item.description: Abstract Context compaction replaces history with summaries, paying for their generation and changing an agent’s subsequent work.
